questions.q: How does the customer-segment extract build the CustomerSegment column?
options: By filtering on Sales.SalesTerritory.Group
By joining to a separate CustomerSegment table that doesn't exist
By checking whether CustomerID is an even or odd number
CASE WHEN c.StoreID IS NOT NULL THEN 'Store/Reseller' ELSE 'Individual' END
questions.explain: The CASE expression checks StoreID directly, matching the real Sales.Customer schema.

questions.q: What does WHERE soh.Status = 5 restrict both extracts to?
options: Orders placed exactly 5 days ago
Orders from territory ID 5
Shipped (completed) sales orders only
Cancelled orders
questions.explain: Status = 5 is AdventureWorks2012's code for a shipped order, used so both stakeholder pages agree on what counts as a completed sale.

questions.q: Why do header-level columns like OrderDate repeat multiple times in the extract output?
options: Joining in Sales.SalesOrderDetail causes row fan-out -- one row per order line, repeating the header columns
DISTINCT was forgotten and should always be added here
It's a bug in the JOIN syntax
AdventureWorks2012 stores OrderDate redundantly on purpose
questions.explain: SalesOrderDetail has many rows per SalesOrderID, so the one-to-many join repeats header columns per line -- the expected shape for a line-level extract.

questions.q: Where does the LineTotal dollar amount actually live?
options: Sales.Customer, at the customer level
Sales.SalesOrderDetail.LineTotal, at the order-line level
Sales.SalesOrderHeader, at the order level
Sales.SalesTerritory, at the territory level
questions.explain: The actual revenue figure lives on SalesOrderDetail, which is why the extract joins through it instead of stopping at SalesOrderHeader.

questions.q: Why does this project keep the customer extract and territory extract as two separate T-SQL queries instead of one combined query?
options: It matches the real scenario of two different people independently pulling two different extracts, which Python will later join properly
T-SQL cannot join more than three tables in one query
Power BI requires exactly two separate data sources
SalesTerritory and Customer cannot both be joined to SalesOrderHeader
questions.explain: Keeping them separate mirrors Lesson 1's real scenario and sets up the Python join work in Lesson 6.
